case_name: Guddu vs State Nct Of Delhi
facts_of_case: The victim died in her matrimonial home. Appellant Guddu was convicted under Section 304-B and 498-A IPC. He was sentenced to RI for 10 years, fine of Rs.30,000/-, and SI for 6 months. Appellant Sudha was convicted under Section 498-A IPC and sentenced to RI for 3 years, fine of Rs.10,000/-, and SI for 9 months.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to prove how the death of the victim occurred within less than 6 months of the marriage at the matrimonial home.
legal_principles.held: The burden under Section 304-B of the IPC has been shifted upon the accused and it is for the accused to have proved how the death of the victim occurred within less than 6 months of the marriage at the matrimonial home.

legal_principles.principle: The prosecution must prove that there was a demand in connection with dowry to establish an offence under Section 304-B of the IPC.
legal_principles.held: it is incumbent upon the prosecution to have proved that there was a demand in connection with dowry which is wholly missing in this case.

legal_principles.principle: The court may invoke the presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act.
legal_principles.held: Presumption under Section 113-B of the Indian Evidence Act has been rightly invoked by the trial Judge.

outcome.final_order: The sentences were to run concurrently for both the appellants.
